title: SLO-driven ingest segmenter and tenant soft-quota for audit logs
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Summary: Implement an SLO-driven ingest segmenter (a lightweight pre-indexing stage) that groups audit events into bounded segments by tenant and logical admin scope, emits short-lived indexing metadata to the hot index, and routes older segments into staged cold segments for batched compaction or archive. This ticket also adds a tenant 'soft-quota' governor that applies backpressure and adaptive sampling during bursts, surfaced to admins via RBAC v2-scoped alerts and SSO/SAML-linked audit dashboards.

Goals:
- Reduce per-tenant hot index write amplification and storage costs while preserving queryability for recent events (7–14 days configurable).
- Ensure admin actions (RBAC v2 changes, SSO/SAML auth events) remain queryable with high fidelity for 30 days before archival.
- Provide safe backpressure that avoids data loss: soft-quota causes sampling + delayed write to cold stage, not drop.
- Give tenant admins (via RBAC v2 roles) observability and self-serve controls over their quota and retention within limits.

Design decisions & trade-offs (high level):
- Segmenter vs continuous stream rewrite: segmenter introduces a bounded-stage that allows more efficient per-segment compaction and reduces index shard fanout at ingest time. Trade-off: added complexity in ingest path and slightly increased write latency (~5–15ms median under load). Considered but rejected continuous rewrite because it increases tail latency and complicates per-tenant TTL.
- Soft-quota (adaptive sampling + staged cold path) vs hard-throttle: soft-quota preserves customer data (sampled) and keeps platform reliable; hard-throttle risks dropped audit records and escalations.
- Storage tiers: hot index (0–14d), warm compact segments (15–90d), cold archive (S3/GCS) with optional full-text index snapshots for compliance customers. We favor cost-first retention for normal tenants and retention-override APIs for enterprise seats.

Implementation notes:
- New ingest component: ingest-segmenter service (sidecar in chronicle ingestion pipeline). Responsibilities: segment routing, per-tenant token bucket estimation, short-lived KV for segment metadata, and emit 'segment-manifest' events to control plane.
- Quota algorithm: combine a per-tenant baseline with burst credits that decay over time. When CPU or index write SLOs approach threshold, segmenter switches to progressive sampling with deterministic reservoir to preserve head events (RBAC-admin/SAML-critical events prioritized).
- Indexing pipeline: create 'segment' document type in hot index that references compressed event blob(s) stored in blobstore. Hot index stores only recent segments metadata + first N events for quick queries. A background compactor will decompress, re-index, and merge segments into warm indexes on off-peak windows.
- RBAC v2 integration: segmenter will attach RBAC context (role, admin-change marker) to segment metadata so queries can perform fast-role-based filtering. Ensure RBAC v2 changes themselves are recorded immutably and pinned for full fidelity in warm index for 30 days by default.
- SSO/SAML correlation: enrich segments with SAML assertion hash and auth_event_id to speed up cross-join between auth events and subsequent admin actions. This prevents expensive joins at query time.

Progress & current status:
- Feb 10: Proposal drafted and reviewed with Security and Observability (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUD/Segmenter+Proposal).
- Feb 18: Design review with infra and runtime accepted; action items assigned to this ticket.
- Feb 25: Prototype of segment manifest and blobstore layout completed (internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4826).
- Mar 01: Load test harness run against prototype (dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest-seg/proto-load). Observed 18% reduction in hot index write amplification at p95 when segments size tuned to 32–64KiB.
- Mar 04: Security requested data-flow diagram and threat model updates (attached), flagged encryption-in-transit validation for SAML assertion hashes.

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Added runtime complexity may increase incident surface. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout, canary @ 5% of tenants, clear rollback plan to bypass segmenter and stream directly.
- Risk: Compliance customers require full fidelity for longer retention. Mitigation: retention-override with enterprise SLA and extra cold-archive replicas + immutable snapshots.
- Risk: Sampling could omit critical admin events during extreme bursts. Mitigation: deterministic reservoir prioritized by RBAC-admin, severity tags, and SAML-linked event correlation.

Next steps / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement segmenter sidecar with unit & integration tests; feature flag gating.
- End-to-end test: ingest → hot index → compactor → warm index → cold archive with no data loss on canary tenants.
- Dashboard metrics for segment sizes, sampled rate, per-tenant quota usage, and SLO impact.
- Documentation: runbook for rollout/rollback, Confluence design, API docs for tenant admins (console + programmatic controls).

- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest-seg/proto-load
